doc: arrowKind cases were executed from the-bastion's backend/reconcile.py (arrow_shape) on element field combinations drawn from tests/test_reconcile.py's TestFlowRoutes. arrowFields cases were executed by calling the-bastion's frontend/src/render.ts buildScene() end to end and reading the roundness/elbowed fields it wrote onto the arrow it drew for each shape word — the write side of arrowKind, and the exact matrix frontend/src/render.test.mjs checks ('the two fields Excalidraw uses are written from one word'): sharp writes {roundness: null} and no elbowed key at all; curved writes {roundness: {type: 2}} and no elbowed key; elbow writes {roundness: null, elbowed: true}. arrowElement cases for the 'poll' flow (an elbow that doubles back through six points) and the 'read' flow (a straight two-point line) were read directly off the arrow elements buildScene() drew for frontend/src/render.test.mjs's own GEOMETRY fixture.

cases.name: neither field set reads as sharp
elbowed true reads as elbow even with roundness also set
elbowed false with roundness set still reads as curved
roundness explicitly null reads as sharp
an odd truthy roundness value still reads as curved
elbowed alone with no roundness reads as elbow
no shape recorded (an older geometry) writes the sharp fields
sharp writes roundness null and no elbowed key
curved writes a type-2 roundness and no elbowed key
elbow writes elbowed true and roundness null
the poll flow's points, relativised and sized to their extent
the read flow's points, relativised and sized to their extent
a single point has zero extent (an extrapolation past what render.ts ever receives)
